items.title: John Pope Interview, 1959-05-01
items.q: Yes, I remember him in the early days. I think he used to play Yanmobili. He used to come over here and play for the next school.

ctx.x: Did you ever hear Joe Oliver? They called him King Oliver later?

Joe Oliver? Yes, I remember him in the early days. I think he used to play Yanmobili. He used to come over here and play for the next school. That's been quite a while now. Oh, yes, a long time. Yeah, I'm going way back. I remember quite a few out of the audience, but I just can't recall them now because I'm not prepared.
Did you ever hear Freddie Caput? No, I haven't. No, I haven't. From New Orleans. No, I haven't.

items.title: John Pope Interview, 1959-05-01
items.q: INTERVIEWEE: Joe Oliver? Yes, I remember him in the early days. I think he used to play Yanmobili. He used to come over here and play for the next school.

ctx.x: Remember Buddy Petit? Did he play over here? Who's that Buddy Petit? No, I don't remember. Or Chris Pelley? No, I don't remember that. There's another man, an old time trumpet that told me once about your father, Bunk Johnson. Did you ever meet him? No, I don't think that either. Bunk Johnson. No, I don't think that either. They tell me once that your father, I've been told that they would play on Mardi Gras day, the boat would come in with some of the organizations. Did they do that?
Do you remember? Yes, I did. King, queen, they would come in.

I played all those. People told me that your father used to be famous that the word they used, they played a lot of flourishes, like bugle calls or something that the king would come in. That's right. What kind of bugle calls were they? What was white?
